verification.summary: PR #106 merged as f9544a40 after the same 57a8cde3 CI head passed on an unchanged rerun. The first run had one unnamed Node contract failure hidden by the bounded output tail; the rerun passed all checks and the local full profile had already passed. Production then matched all 16 changed runtime files by SHA-256, enabled the snapshot feature, passed the 80-template shadow, 26/14 SimC matrix, real reused task, service/log/timer checks and post-merge 2096-test backend profile. Local main, origin/main and cloud runtime are aligned for their separate commit/runtime identities.

smoke.summary: The 80-template shadow is verified with all 40 specializations classified as 26 supported and 14 unsupported, 8 ready and 72 explicitly blocked loadouts, 4 ready and 4 policy-unsupported snapshots, stable generation 32 and no snapshot compilation block. rollback.summary: The active Manifest remains generation 32 and unchanged. Both candidate services are isolated transient units, the feature can be disabled with WOW_SIMULATION_SNAPSHOT_V1_ENABLED=0, append-only rows can remain dormant, and the pre-migration backup remains present under the Phase 3 backup root.

runtimeEvidence.interpretation: Fail-closed behavior was correct. Candidate data proved that the archived 55 partial exact references are distributed across 72 templates and therefore cannot be required to produce ready snapshots in Phase 3. The four clean supported templates also exposed compatibility profile ordering drift for follow-up diagnosis.

The corrected 26/14 classification gate passed while all four supported clean loadouts still failed byte parity. Focused comparison traced the remaining drift to the legacy Resolver serializer's alphabetical slot iteration versus the target CANONICAL_GEAR_SLOTS order. The compatibility facade now normalizes both set-like option values and slot order before snapshot compilation.

The 80-template shadow, exact 26/14 SimC matrix and first sealed snapshot task all passed. Replaying the same canonical snapshot under a different guest exposed that stochastic SimC metrics can produce a second result identity while the snapshot has a one-to-one append-only result binding. The Runner now reuses a validated existing terminal result before execution instead of rerunning SimC or reporting a false storage failure.

The final immutable runtime head passes the complete candidate contract. Repeated tasks reload and reuse the exact terminal result bound to the canonical snapshot; they do not rerun SimC, do not create a second result row and do not leak private execution payloads.

Production executes the same immutable runtime bytes proven by the candidate. The live task reuses the previously bound exact result, the active Manifest remains generation 32, and global data health remains literally partial under independent owners.

risks.detail: All templates containing any of the 55 archived partial references remain explicitly blocked; the final candidate classifies all 80 templates without silent fallback.
All four clean supported template snapshots compile byte-identically after canonical set-like option and slot-order normalization.
Global /api/data/health is independently partial and will not be represented as a Phase 3 pass.

cleanup.scope: The published task branch and four Phase 3 candidate directories were removed after verified merge and production parity. The valid predeploy rollback backup remains; the failed first backup attempt was removed.

summary: Strict Phase 3 is archived after immutable candidate 84f16ef6, full verification, PR #106, merge f9544a40, production deployment and three-party closure. Exact ResolvedLoadout and immutable SimulationSnapshot identities now own canonical task execution; one append-only terminal result is bound per snapshot and repeated tasks reuse it without rerunning SimC or leaking private execution payloads. Live 80-template and 40-spec classification, 26/14 SimC policy, migration idempotency, rollback, resource, service and parity gates pass. Global /api/data/health remains literally partial under independent owners and is carried into Phase 4.
